title: Program ENIAC: Our New Touch-Screen Exhibit
description:
Meet the newest exhibit at the Vintage Computer Federation museum: a touch-screen kiosk where you get to program ENIAC, the room-sized computer of 1946. I built it as a docent, and in this video I'll walk you through it, from the live attract screen to the full Squares mission.

Chapters
0:00 Meet the kiosk
0:53 Explore ENIAC
2:23 Keeping ENIAC alive
3:47 The first programmers
4:06 Mission 1: Squares
6:37 Only at the museum
7:04 The finale
7:44 Come see it

Come see it at the Vintage Computer Federation, InfoAge Science and History Museums, Wall, New Jersey: https://vcfed.org

Credits
Exhibit by Nick DeMarco, Docent and Exhibit Developer, Vintage Computer Federation.
Built on Brian L. Stuart's ENIAC simulator (Drexel University): https://www.cs.drexel.edu/~bls96/eniac/simulator.html and https://github.com/blstuart/eniac-simulator
Period photographs: U.S. Army Photo, public domain (via Wikimedia Commons).
Music: "Hot Swing", "In Your Arms" and "Long Stroll" by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com)
